ai.name: Tencent Hy Team
ai.hook: Tencent drops Hy3, a 295B open-weight model that beats models 2-5x its size.
insights: **295B MoE** with only **21B active parameters** and **256K context**, Apache 2.0 licensed
Runs natively on **vLLM** with up to **2.95x speedups** on both NVIDIA and AMD hardware
Positioned as a direct rival to **GLM-5.2** in the open model race
ai.for_you: Not something to run on a laptop, but worth knowing open models keep closing the gap with frontier closed models, which matters for keeping agency costs down if you ever self-host for PT clients wary of sending data to US clouds.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Only real open-weight model release today, confirmed across two independent sources

ai.name: Simon Willison
ai.hook: Ships sqlite-utils 4.0 almost entirely written by Claude Fable, for $149 in API costs.
insights: Used **Claude Code on iPhone** to do a final pre-release review of a real production library
Cost breakdown made public: **~$149.25** for a full major-version release cycle
Feature scope grew mid-process (compound foreign key support) because the agent kept finding more to fix
ai.for_you: This is the clearest real-world proof point yet of what 'AI does a real ship-quality software task end to end' costs in dollars, use this exact framing when pitching PT SMB clients on what an agentic workflow can replace versus a junior dev.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Concrete dollar figure and workflow, rare and useful over vague model-launch hype

ai.name: Martin Alderson
ai.role: Blog post · Hacker News (408 pts, 251 comments)
ai.hook: Argues GLM-5.2's price/performance is the start of an AI margin collapse.
insights: Open models like **GLM-5.2** now close enough to frontier that API resellers can't sustain current markups
Top HN story of the day by a wide margin, 251 comments of pushback and agreement
Thesis: whoever builds thin wrappers on frontier model APIs gets squeezed first
ai.for_you: Directly relevant to your AI agency's pricing model, if margin compression is real, differentiate on integration/workflow ownership for PT SMBs rather than on model access, because that part is about to get commoditized fast.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Highest engagement item across all sources today, directly threatens agency-model economics

ai.name: Natalia Quintero
ai.role: Head of Consulting · Every (AI & I podcast)
ai.hook: A non-technical consultant now builds internal tools with Codex instead of buying SaaS.
insights: Automated her own **CRM setup** and built a medical-care management portal without being a developer
Every still pays for **Attio and Asana** rather than vibe-coding replacements, drawing a real line on where AI-built tools stop making sense
Uses an internal AI agent ('Claudie') as a project manager that still needs human oversight
ai.for_you: This is your exact user profile, a non-technical operator building real internal tooling with AI. Steal her before/after workflow as a case study you can literally replicate for a PT SMB client's ops.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Most directly analogous persona to Pedro of anything in today's sources

ai.name: Vercel / Guillermo Rauch
ai.hook: Vercel bets agents and models are splitting into separate layers you must design for.
insights: Vercel's **eve** framework treats agents as a distinct software category, not just a chat wrapper on a model
New concepts pushed: **skills, sandboxes, and agent-readable websites** as first-class design targets
Argument: coordination (routing, memory, observability) is now the hard problem, not raw model capability
ai.for_you: When you scope agency projects for PT SMBs, start separating 'which model' from 'what does the agent actually do and remember' in your proposals, clients are starting to expect that distinction from vendors who know what they're doing.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Recurring theme across three sources today (Latent Space, TechCrunch, AINews) on agent architecture shift

ai.name: Genesis (Evan Feinberg & Sergey Edunov)
ai.hook: Diffusion models now predict how proteins physically flex to bind drugs, not just static poses.
insights: New model **PEARL** models protein flexibility during ligand binding, previously computationally intractable
Agentic system **SAPPHIRE** acts like a chemist: forms hypotheses, reads literature, proposes next candidates
Argues the industry benchmark (2Å RMSD) is largely meaningless ('slop')
ai.for_you: No direct action here, filed for awareness, this is a good talking point if a PT biotech/pharma prospect ever comes up, but not core to your SMB agency work.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Genuinely novel technical development, distinct from the usual LLM news cycle

build_this.name: OfficeCLI
build_this.what_it_is: A CLI tool letting AI agents directly read and edit Microsoft Office files (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
build_this.why_try_it: Most PT SMBs live in Excel and Word for invoicing, proposals, reports. Wire this into a Claude Code or Codex workflow this week and you have a concrete agency demo: 'AI that fills in your monthly report from raw data' without exporting to some SaaS dashboard they'll never adopt.

build_this.name: Ternlight
build_this.what_it_is: A 7MB embedding model that runs entirely in-browser via WASM, no server needed.
build_this.why_try_it: For the yoga/meditation platform, this could power on-device semantic search over class transcripts or journaling entries with zero backend cost or latency, worth a quick prototype this week to see if it's fast enough for a real search box.

build_this.name: Code Cleanliness vs Coding Agents study
build_this.what_it_is: Controlled study measuring whether messy vs clean codebases actually change coding agent performance.
build_this.why_try_it: Read this before your next vibe-coding session on the micro-SaaS idea, it'll tell you whether it's worth the extra time to keep your prototype code clean or if agents handle mess fine, directly affects how you spend your limited building hours.
